• Perception is the process of attaining awareness or understanding of sensory information. Hallucination and illusion are both disorders of perceptions.
  • Hallucination is a perception without a real stimuli/stimulus. For example, a person may complain that some insect is crawling on the body but there is no such insect seen in reality (tactile hallucination). A person may see (visual), hear (auditory), smell (olfactory), or taste (gustatory) things that do not exist outside his/her mind.
  • On contrary, Illusion refers to false perception of existing stimuli/stimulus. For example, a person may perceive a rope on the road as a snake. Here the rope is considered a stimulus, but the person perceived it as a snake (wrong perception).
